# 08 Lay out nested control-flow block bounding boxes

## Outcome

`layoutSequence` computes each block's bounding rectangle: horizontal extent from the leftmost to
the rightmost participant lane in its (recursive) `participantsTouched` set, vertical extent
covering its header, every branch's divider + label, and its full nested body — recursively, so a
block containing blocks reserves enough vertical space for their bounding boxes too, and its own
box fully encloses each child's.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A single `loop` wrapping two messages between two adjacent participants produces a
  `PositionedBlock` whose x-range exactly spans those two participants' lanes (with padding) and
  whose y-range encloses the header label plus both messages.
- [ ] An `alt` with two branches produces one `PositionedBlock` with two divider y-positions (one
  per branch after the first) and per-branch condition-label positions.
- [ ] A block touching participants that are not adjacent in lane order (e.g. lanes 1 and 3, with
  lane 2 declared but untouched by this block) still spans from lane 1 to lane 3, covering the
  untouched lane 2 visually — matches Mermaid's own behavior.
- [ ] Nested blocks (`loop` > `alt` > `par`, three levels) each produce a `PositionedBlock` whose
  box fully contains its child's box with visible padding between the frames.
- [ ] Every message inside any block still gets a y-coordinate strictly increasing in document
  order across the whole diagram (block nesting doesn't disturb the global top-to-bottom time
  axis established in ticket 03).
- [ ] `PositionedSequenceDiagram.height`/`width` account for the extra space every block frame,
  divider, and label reserves.

## Test seam

`layoutSequence(model: SequenceModel, options: { measureText: TextMeasurer }):
PositionedSequenceDiagram` — unit level, pure function, extending ticket 03's fixtures with
block-bearing `SequenceModel` fixtures.
